question: Why does one who sees all realities as one's own self perceive no sameness among them?
premises: Realities are truly real in their own nature
They appear as forms of one's own self
Seeing them as self-nature removes imposed uniformity
inference: For one who perceives realities as forms of the self, there is no mere sameness among them.
plain_english: For one who sees realities as true forms of one's own self, there is no sameness among them.
